ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the lower non-inverting input terminal “+” of the operational amplifier is connected to the input voltage ui; the node where the upper inverting input terminal “-” is located is directly connected to the output terminal uo through a feedback wire; this inverting input node is also connected to ground through a resistor. Reasoning: Treat the op-amp as an ideal op-amp and negative feedback exists, then the virtual short holds, and the inverting terminal voltage V- equals the non-inverting terminal voltage V+. Since the non-inverting terminal V+ = ui, and the inverting terminal node is directly connected to the output terminal by a wire, V- = uo. Therefore uo = ui, and the closed-loop voltage gain Au = uo/ui = 1.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: the + input receives ui, while the output uo is directly connected back to the - input; the resistor from that node goes to ground. Treat the op-amp as ideal with negative feedback, so V- = V+. Because V- is shorted to uo and V+ = ui, conclude uo = ui. Therefore the voltage gain is 1.
